observation.visible_scene: An outdoor, low-angle view of a weathered two-story wooden building with peeling grey paint, vertical plank siding, dark window openings, metal balcony railings, and a pale downspout running vertically on the left. A thick wooden utility pole stands in the foreground, center-right, and an arm from it holds a street lamp whose disc-shaped shade glows bright orange/amber with the bulb lit. A few tree leaves intrude at the right edge of the frame.
visible_changes: The camera gradually widens its field of view (a slow zoom-out / pull-back): the lamp shade, the pole, and the roof-eave brackets all occupy fewer pixels by the last frame, while more of the scene is revealed at the margins — a left building corner with its own balcony railing on the left, a dark awning/roofline and blue vent boxes along the bottom, and a patch of pale sky at the top-left.

The glowing lamp shade stays lit at a steady orange intensity and keeps a fixed tilt and orientation relative to its mounting arm; it does not swing, flicker, or change shape within the excerpt, only shifting slightly in image position as the framing widens.
The building, pole, downspout, and railings are otherwise static structures; the only apparent non-camera motion is a small positional shift of the leaves at the right edge between frames.
Relative layout is preserved throughout: the lamp disc remains left of the pole, the pole remains right of the downspout, and the eaves remain above the windows.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the lamp was already lit before this segment or remains lit after it, and whether it ever flickers outside these frames.
Whether the camera motion continues, stops, or reverses beyond the crop boundaries.
The cause of the slight leaf movement (wind or just reframing).
uncertain_details: The exact nature of the framing change (optical zoom-out versus a physical dolly/pull-back plus slight tilt) cannot be distinguished from these samples.
The small drift of the lamp disc and the leaf shifts are minor and may be partly attributable to the changing field of view rather than independent object motion.
